provenance.instrument: Borough of Phoenixville Zoning Ordinance (form-based), Chapter 27 Zoning as enacted by Ord. No. 2025-2410, as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: The former Chapter 27 (Ord. 2227 of 2013 as amended) 'was repealed by Ord. No. 2025-2410, 8/12/2025', which enacted the current chapter with the ADU special exception (27-301.2B(2)(d)). 27-301 was amended by Ord. No. 2025-2415 (10-14-2025) and Ord. No. 2026-2424 (3-10-2026), and 27-405 by Ord. No. 2026-2424. eCode360 header: legislation through 09-08-2026. New Laws (read 2026-11-13): none.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 header on 2026-11-13: 'Includes legislation through 09-08-2026.' No new laws pending.
checks: An accessory dwelling unit is a special exception (Zoning Hearing Board) in RI, MI, NC, CD and MG. It is not listed in TC or I (27-301.2B(1) table)
One ADU, accessory to a single-family dwelling: a detached house, a twin or a townhouse (27-301.2B(2)(d)1))
The owner of the lot must live in one of the two dwellings 'in perpetuity' (27-301.2B(2)(d)2))

Inside the house: at most 25% of the existing house's habitable floor area. As an addition: an increase of at most 25% of that area. In an accessory building: the accessory building limits, a building FOOTPRINT at most two thirds of the house's footprint, not two thirds of its floor area (27-301.2B(2)(d)6), 27-404.2B(1))

An accessory building may be at most two stories or two thirds of the actual house height, whichever is less (20 ft for a 30 ft house, 23 ft only for a 35 ft house). With a one-story house it may not be taller than the house. No more than two accessory buildings on a lot (27-404.2B(2), (3))
A detached ADU may not be in the required front yard. Its own entrance, not in the front facade of the house (27-301.2B(2)(d)4), 5))

The ADU meets the setback and coverage rules of the district for its type. In the RI chart an accessory building is 8 ft from the rear line and 5 ft from the side, or attached. The detached house is 25 ft rear, 5 ft side, 80% impervious (27-301.2B(2)(d)3), Attachment 1)
Public electric, water and sewer, connected to the house's existing systems (27-301.2B(2)(d)11))

Parking: 1 space for the ADU ('Accessory dwelling unit 1 space'), 3 in all with a detached house or townhouse. The ADU may not remove any existing off-street space. The Borough may adjust the minimum under 27-405.3 (27-405.2C, 27-301.2B(2)(d)10))
Registered with the Borough every year. The registration ends when the lot is sold, and the new owner may register again (27-301.2B(2)(d)8))
A concept plan to scale with the building permit application (27-301.2B(2)(d)9))
MI, NC, CD and MG allow the same residential building types as RI, and the RI standards may be modified by up to 25% to fit the streetscape (Attachment 1)
Lots under one acre take infill standards from the block: the minimum lot area is the median lot area on the block face, side yards match an adjacent lot (27-301.1A)
In RI no new building type or residential use may be introduced in a block unless the tract is at least eight acres (27-301.1D). That limits a duplex, not the ADU
Residential uses are permitted by right in TC, but TC does not list the ADU

The RI chart sets a minimum building spacing of 10 ft for single-family detached and twin houses. Whether it reaches an accessory building on the same lot is not clear, since the chart also lets accessory buildings be attached (Attachment 1)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Borough of Phoenixville. Read on eCode360 in a browser, one section print view at a time. The use tables were read from the page as displayed. The district specifications are an image PDF attachment, read page by page. Searched the definitions for accessory dwelling, accessory building, duplex and short-term. The index note's 'TC' in the ADU district list is not borne out by the table, which marks RI, MI, NC, CD and MG. The 27-405.2C table has an 'Accessory dwelling unit 1 space' row (a first reading missed it). Chester County Planning Commission material (cross-check only) has nothing on Phoenixville ADUs. The earlier town survey has no Phoenixville entry.

term.note: 'ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT (ADU) An accessory dwelling proposed within an existing principal single-family dwelling, attached to an existing principal single-family dwelling by way of addition, or wholly and exclusively within an accessory building on the same lot as a principal single-family dwelling.' Internal, attached and detached ADUs.

status.note: 'The uses listed below are permitted by special exception in the zoning districts as indicated below.' The ADU row is marked in RI, MI, NC, CD and MG.

path.note: Zoning Hearing Board special exception, with the ADU standards of 27-301.2B(2)(d). Then a building permit with a concept plan and annual registration.

fallback_path.note: A unit that fails the standards, or one in TC or I, needs a variance.

value.name: Duplex (two units, one over the other)
value.conditions: Residential uses are by right. A duplex is two units in one building, separated by a floor and ceiling. RI chart: lot 2,000 sq ft, 40 ft wide, 5 ft side, 20 ft rear, 35 ft, 90% impervious. In RI a duplex may not be introduced in a block that has none unless the tract is eight acres or more.
value.note: Not an ADU. Whether an existing house may be converted to a duplex is for the zoning officer.

zoning_districts.note: Special exception table, read as displayed. TC and I are not marked.

building_types.note: 'One ADU may be permitted as an accessory use to a single-family dwelling, including a single-family detached dwelling, a twin dwelling or a townhouse dwelling.'

existing_structure_only.note: An internal or attached ADU needs an existing house. A detached ADU may be a new accessory building.

historic_bypass.note: No historic path for an ADU. Adaptive reuse of historic buildings is a separate conditional use.

value.condition: An internal ADU is built within an existing house, an attached ADU as an addition to an existing house. Its size is measured from the house's habitable floor area before construction.

Detached ADU: the accessory building footprint is at most two thirds of the house footprint. Height at most two stories or two thirds of the house height, whichever is less, and no taller than a one-story house. At most two accessory buildings on the lot.
A detached ADU may not be in the required front yard. An entrance separate from the house's, not in the house's front facade.
Public electric, water and sewer, connected to the house's existing systems.
Registered with the Borough every year. The registration ends when the lot is conveyed. A concept plan to scale with the building permit application.
The ADU may not remove any existing off-street parking on the lot.

types_allowed.note: Internal, attached (an addition) and detached ('wholly and exclusively within an accessory building'). A unit over a garage is not named. 'Wholly and exclusively' may be read to bar a unit that shares a building with a garage. Ask.

max_sqft.note: No square foot cap. Share caps only, and one bedroom.

max_share_internal.note: 'Internal ADU — Not to exceed 25% of existing principal dwelling's habitable floor area prior to construction.' 'Attached ADU — Not to exceed 25% increase of the existing principal dwelling's habitable floor area prior to construction.'

max_share_accessory_building.note: 'Detached ADU — Per accessory building size limits'. 'The building footprint shall be no more than 2/3 that of the principal building.' A share of the house's footprint, not of its floor area. The tool shows it as a share of the house.

max_height_ft.note: 'The building height shall be no more than two stories or 2/3 the principal building height, whichever is less. If the principal building is one story, an accessory building shall not exceed the height of the principal building.' The cap is two thirds of the actual house height. 23 ft is only the figure for a 35 ft house, the district maximum. For a 30 ft house the cap is 20 ft.

height_capped_at_house.note: At most two thirds of the house height, which is lower than the house.

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: ADUs meet 'all building setback and coverage requirements of the underlying zoning district and per ADU type'. The district chart gives accessory buildings their own rear and side setbacks.

setback_front_ft.note: 'A detached ADU may not be located within the required front yard.' The front line is the block's build-to line.

owner_occupancy.note: 'One of the dwellings shall be occupied, in perpetuity, by the owner of the lot on which both dwellings are located.'

max_adus.note: 'One ADU may be permitted as an accessory use to a single-family dwelling'.

short_term_rental_banned.note: No short-term rental rule in Chapter 27.

spaces_required.note: Table for residential developments of four or fewer dwellings, last row: 'Accessory dwelling unit 1 space'. The ADU may not remove existing off-street spaces (27-301.2B(2)(d)10)). 27-405.3 lets the Borough adjust the minimum (shared parking and the like).

total_on_site.note: 'Single-family detached 2 spaces per dwelling unit' (townhouse also 2) plus 1 for the ADU. A twin is 1 or 2 by bedrooms, so the total for a twin is 2 or 3.

new_connection_required.note: 'All ADUs shall be served by public electric, water and sewer services, connected to the principal dwelling's existing systems for each.'

min_lot_sqft.note: Chart figure. For lots under one acre the minimum is the median lot area on the block face. Twin 3,000 sq ft, townhouse 2,000.

setback_side_ft.note: Single-family detached. Lots under one acre match an adjacent side yard (27-301.1A(3)).

setback_rear_ft.note: Single-family detached. Twin and townhouse 20 ft.

separation_ft.note: 'Min. Building Spacing 10 ft.' (twin 10 ft). Whether it binds an accessory building on the same lot is not settled.
